meta.eyebrow: Product Portfolio · Built as a system of labs
meta.title: Six labs. One product mind across the whole stack.
meta.intro: Each lab is a discipline I work in end-to-end — from the founder's first bet to the data model, the architecture, the AI, and the product people actually use. Step into any lab to explore what it ships.

labs.name: Founder Lab
labs.desc: Zero-to-one bets — the ventures, pitches, and operating systems built before there was a product to manage.
labs.blurb: Where ideas become companies. Founder Lab holds the early-stage ventures, the napkin-to-narrative pitches, and the operating frameworks used to take a bet from conviction to a fundable, buildable plan.

products.name: Northwind
products.tagline: An operating system for lenders who want to launch a credit product in weeks, not quarters.
products.what:
Northwind started as a thesis: most lenders don't have a technology problem, they have a launch problem. The product packages origination, decisioning, and servicing into a single configurable rail so a new credit product can go from board approval to first disbursal in under 60 days.

Founder Lab is where the bet was framed — the market sizing, the wedge, the first ten design partners, and the narrative that turned a deck into a seed round.
features: Underserved mid-market lenders ignored by core-banking incumbents.
Ten hand-picked design partners co-building the v1.
A single story that ran from cold intro to term sheet.

products.name: Atlas Collective
products.tagline: A venture studio model for spinning enterprise tools out of repeatable internal playbooks.
products.what:
Atlas Collective is the framework for turning hard-won internal playbooks into standalone products. Rather than one big bet, it's a portfolio motion: identify a repeatable operational pain, productize the fix, and spin it out with its own P&L.

This lab captures the operating cadence — how bets are sourced, staffed, killed, or doubled-down on.
features: A scored pipeline of operational pains worth productizing.
Clear kill/continue criteria at each funding step.
Common identity, billing, and data layer across spin-outs.

products.name: Ironwood
products.tagline: A carbon-accounting layer for supply chains that treats emissions as a first-class ledger.
products.what:
Ironwood is an early concept exploring what supply-chain carbon accounting looks like if you build it like a financial ledger — double-entry, auditable, and reconciled, rather than a once-a-year spreadsheet estimate.

Founder Lab holds the problem framing, the regulatory read, and the prototype used to test appetite with three enterprise buyers.
features: Every emission is a posted, reconcilable entry.
Defensible numbers for regulators and buyers alike.
Three enterprise interviews validating willingness to pay.

labs.name: Analytics Lab
labs.desc: Decisions made legible — metric trees, dashboards, and the measurement systems that tell a business the truth.
labs.blurb: Numbers that earn trust. Analytics Lab is where raw events become metric trees, experiments, and dashboards a leadership team can actually steer with — measurement designed to change decisions, not just decorate slides.

products.name: Pulse
products.tagline: An executive cockpit that turns a sprawl of product events into three numbers that matter.
products.what:
Pulse is a decision dashboard, not a data dump. It collapses hundreds of tracked events into a tight metric tree, surfaces the two or three movements that actually changed the business this week, and explains why.

Analytics Lab is where the metric model was designed — the north star, its inputs, and the guardrails that stop teams from gaming a single number.
features: A north star decomposed into inputs teams can own.
Automatic surfacing of what changed and why.

products.name: Cohort
products.tagline: Retention analysis that finally answers 'which users come back, and what made them.'
products.what:
Cohort makes retention investigable. Instead of a flat curve, it lets a team slice survival by acquisition source, first-week behavior, and feature adoption — then quantifies which early actions actually predict long-term return.

This lab covers the analytical framing and the experiment design behind every claim.
features: Group users by what they did, not just when they joined.
The early actions that predict retention.
Every insight ships with a testable hypothesis.

products.name: Signal
products.tagline: Anomaly detection for business metrics that pages a human only when it's worth it.
products.what:
Signal watches the metric tree and learns each line's normal rhythm, so it can tell a genuine anomaly from ordinary noise. When something real breaks, it routes a concise, contextual alert to the right owner — and stays quiet otherwise.

Analytics Lab holds the detection model and the false-positive tuning that makes the alerts trusted.
features: Knows the difference between a dip and a Tuesday.
The right person, with context, not a firehose.

products.name: Dashboard Studio
products.tagline: A drag-and-drop dashboard builder — KPI cards, charts, data profiling, theming, and export, with data that never leaves the browser.
products.what: A drag-and-drop dashboard builder — KPI cards, charts, data profiling, theming, and export, with data that never leaves the browser.
features: KPI cards and charts assembled visually.
Understand a dataset before you chart it.

labs.name: AI Lab
labs.desc: AI-native products done honestly — copilots, RAG, evals, and guardrails with a cost model that survives contact.
labs.blurb: AI that ships and holds up. AI Lab is where use-cases get framed, retrieval gets designed, and outputs get evaluated — copilots and agents built with guardrails, eval harnesses, and an honest unit-economics model from day one.

products.name: Mirror
products.tagline: A collector copilot that drafts the next conversation and explains exactly why.
products.what:
Mirror sits beside a recovery agent and proposes the next-best action — what to say, which offer to extend, when to call — grounded in the account's real history. Crucially, every suggestion carries its reasoning, so a human stays accountable.

AI Lab covers the retrieval design, the eval harness that scores suggestions, and the guardrails that keep it inside policy.
features: Every recommendation cites the account facts behind it.
Hard limits the model cannot talk its way around.

products.name: Synthesis
products.tagline: Document understanding that reads a 200-page contract and answers like an analyst.
products.what:
Synthesis ingests dense enterprise documents — contracts, policies, filings — and lets a user interrogate them in plain language, with answers anchored to the exact clause. It's built to refuse confidently when the document doesn't say.

This lab holds the chunking strategy, the citation model, and the abstention behavior that makes it trustworthy.
features: Answers point back to the source paragraph.
Says 'not in the document' instead of hallucinating.
Handles 200-page documents without losing the thread.

products.name: Oracle
products.tagline: An agentic workflow runner for back-office operations that asks before it acts.
products.what:
Oracle is an exploration into safe agentic automation for operational workflows — reconciliations, exception handling, data fixes. The design principle is human-in-the-loop by default: the agent plans, shows its work, and asks for approval at each consequential step.

AI Lab holds the planning model, the approval UX, and the rollback design.
features: The agent proposes a full plan before touching anything.
Humans sign off on every consequential step.
Every action has a defined, tested rollback.

products.name: AI Collections Cloud
products.tagline: An AI-native recovery platform for lenders — collector copilot, recovery prediction, and next-best-action over a clean domain, data, and event architecture.
products.what: An AI-native recovery platform for lenders — collector copilot, recovery prediction, and next-best-action over a clean domain, data, and event architecture.
features: Drafts the next-best action with the reasoning behind it.
Scores accounts so effort lands where it pays.
Domain, data, and events designed to build on.

products.name: Synthesis — Strategic Framework Engine
products.tagline: An offline strategic-framework builder: import data, configure the analysis, and export to PDF, Markdown, CSV, or JSON — entirely in-browser.
products.what: An offline strategic-framework builder: import data, configure the analysis, and export to PDF, Markdown, CSV, or JSON — entirely in-browser.
features: Configure an analysis, not just a template.
PDF, Markdown, CSV, or JSON in one click.

products.name: NeuralPath — AI Concepts Game
products.tagline: A gamified AI-learning app — concepts, quizzes, XP, streaks, and orchestration flows that teach AI one level at a time.
products.what: A gamified AI-learning app — concepts, quizzes, XP, streaks, and orchestration flows that teach AI one level at a time.
features: Teaches how AI systems fit together.
AI mastery one concept at a time.

labs.name: Architecture Lab
labs.desc: The structure under the surface — context maps, event flows, APIs, and the diagrams engineers can build from.
labs.blurb: Spoken fluently with engineering. Architecture Lab is where products get their skeleton — context diagrams, component boundaries, event flows, and API contracts designed alongside engineers, not thrown over a wall to them.

products.name: Blueprint
products.tagline: The reference architecture behind an AI-native lending platform, drawn to be built.
products.what:
Blueprint is the end-to-end system design for a lending platform — context, components, the events that flow between them, and the integration seams to cores and bureaus. It's deliberately drawn at a fidelity engineering can implement against.

Architecture Lab holds the diagrams, the trade-off log, and the sequencing that turned a whiteboard into a buildable roadmap.
features: Boundaries and actors before any box-and-line detail.
How money, decisions, and data actually move.
Every significant call, written down with its why.

products.name: Keystone
products.tagline: An integration spine that lets a platform speak to any core banking system once.
products.what:
Keystone is the anti-corruption layer between a modern product and the messy reality of legacy cores. Integrate once against Keystone's canonical model, and every downstream feature is insulated from the quirks of the underlying system.

This lab covers the canonical model, the adapter pattern, and the contract tests that keep integrations from rotting.
features: One clean internal language for many dialects.
New cores plug in without touching product code.
Integrations that fail loudly before customers do.

products.name: Lattice
products.tagline: A multi-tenancy model that keeps a hundred lenders isolated without a hundred deployments.
products.what:
Lattice explores how to serve many regulated tenants from shared infrastructure without compromising isolation, residency, or per-tenant configurability. It's the structural answer to 'can we scale to a hundred customers without the ops team drowning.'

Architecture Lab holds the isolation model, the configuration strategy, and the residency design.
features: Hard tenant boundaries on shared infrastructure.

products.name: Enterprise Lending Cloud
products.tagline: A unified LOS + LMS + collections + analytics engine — workflow state machines, EMI math, and deterministic demo data, all client-side.
products.what: A unified LOS + LMS + collections + analytics engine — workflow state machines, EMI math, and deterministic demo data, all client-side.
features: LOS + LMS + collections + analytics in one.

labs.name: Data & Entity Lab
labs.desc: The semantic spine — entity models, master data, and the schemas that make a business legible to software and AI.
labs.blurb: A shared language for the business. Data & Entity Lab is where the domain gets modeled — entities, relationships, master data, and the semantic layer that lets analytics, products, and AI all mean the same thing by the same word.

products.name: Graphmind
products.tagline: A knowledge graph of the lending domain that every product and model reads from.
products.what:
Graphmind is the canonical entity model for the lending domain — borrowers, accounts, obligations, events — expressed as a graph that products, analytics, and AI all share. One definition of 'delinquency,' used everywhere.

Data & Entity Lab holds the ontology, the governance, and the migration that consolidated five conflicting schemas into one.
features: Shared definitions across every team and system.
Schema evolution with review, not surprise.
Consolidated conflicting legacy models into a spine.

products.name: Registry
products.tagline: Master data management that gives every customer exactly one trusted golden record.
products.what:
Registry resolves the same customer appearing five times across five systems into a single golden record — matched, merged, and survivorship-ruled — so downstream products stop arguing about who the customer is.

This lab covers the matching logic, the survivorship rules, and the stewardship workflow for the hard cases.
features: Rules that pick the truest value field by field.
A human workflow for the ambiguous matches.

products.name: Conduit
products.tagline: A streaming data layer that keeps the semantic model fresh in seconds, not nightly.
products.what:
Conduit is the real-time pipeline feeding the entity model — capturing change events from source systems and reconciling them into the graph continuously, so analytics and AI act on minutes-old truth instead of last night's batch.

Data & Entity Lab holds the CDC design, the reconciliation logic, and the freshness SLAs.
features: The graph stays consistent in near-real-time.

products.name: Excel Transformer
products.tagline: A client-side spreadsheet tool to drop, rename, filter, and re-export Excel/CSV files — no data leaves the page.
products.what: A client-side spreadsheet tool to drop, rename, filter, and re-export Excel/CSV files — no data leaves the page.

products.name: Excel Merger
products.tagline: An in-browser tool to merge multiple Excel/CSV files — column strategies, header normalization, and gap-fill — fully offline.
products.what: An in-browser tool to merge multiple Excel/CSV files — column strategies, header normalization, and gap-fill — fully offline.
features: Combine many Excel/CSV files at once.

labs.name: Product Lab
labs.desc: Where it all becomes usable — journeys, flows, hi-fi design, and shipped experiences an engineering team can build.
labs.blurb: The part people actually touch. Product Lab is where strategy, data, and architecture resolve into something usable — journeys, flows, information architecture, and hi-fi design crafted to be both delightful and shippable.

products.name: Loop
products.tagline: A mobile banking experience designed around moments, not menus.
products.what:
Loop reimagines mobile banking around the handful of moments that actually matter — getting paid, paying someone, knowing you're okay — and ruthlessly demotes everything else. The result is an app that feels calm instead of crowded.

Product Lab holds the journey maps, the IA, and the hi-fi flows that shipped to several hundred thousand users.
features: Organized by intent, not by org chart.
The 90% case is one tap; the rest is one more.
Live to hundreds of thousands of users.

products.name: Canvas
products.tagline: A design system that let eight squads ship one coherent product.
products.what:
Canvas is the design system and component library that gave a fast-growing org a shared visual language — tokens, components, and patterns documented well enough that eight squads could ship independently and still look like one product.

This lab covers the token architecture, the contribution model, and the adoption playbook.
features: Squads extend the system without forking it.
How a system actually gets used, not shelved.

products.name: Field
products.tagline: An internal operations console that turns chaotic back-office work into clear queues.
products.what:
Field is the console operations teams live in all day — turning sprawling, ambiguous back-office work into prioritized queues, clear next actions, and visible SLAs. Designed with the people who use it, iterated weekly.

Product Lab holds the workflow design, the prioritization logic, and the usability work behind it.
features: Always a clear next thing to do.
Everyone sees what's at risk, in real time.
Co-designed with the ops team, shipped weekly.
